cells.tense: Care is moving through your hands right now, and none of it is gripping.
cells.act: release it on purpose, not by losing it
cells.ask: Close one finished thing by choice rather than letting it fade — name to yourself what it gave you, put it down, walk on.
cells.core:
Something near you is growing, and you're not standing over it while it happens. You give what's asked and stop there. You can hold what matters without tightening around it, and you can stand at the edge of something you used to run. That's steadiness most people don't have, and it's why what you tend gets room to breathe instead of a schedule.

The next move is to end things on purpose. Let a finished thing close by decision this week rather than by fading — say to yourself what it gave you, put it down, keep going. You're allowed to be the one who loosens the string while the kite is still up. Do that once and you'll feel where your hands don't ache.
cells.sheetLine: Things grow well next to you, and nothing is being clutched.
cells.verb: Tending carefully what is still becoming
cells.place: Where you decide what to set down for good

cells.tense: You will keep holding this together, whatever it costs anyone, including you.
cells.act: let the path show itself instead of forcing clarity
cells.ask: On a matter that hasn't resolved, move from the little you can see and stop there. Don't demand the whole answer before you act.
cells.core:
When something near you is growing, you're ahead of it, smoothing the way before anyone asks — checking, arranging, carrying a shape for it so it can't go wrong. To you it looks like plain love. From the far side, the plant gets its leaves handled to make sure they're fine. You take on what isn't yours to take on, and when you're worn thin, the same thing keeps happening, so something must be wrong with them, or with you.

Stop needing the whole road. On a matter that hasn't resolved, move from what you can see and no further. Leave a detail unwatched. You'll find the situation stands without a hand on it — and find what's left of you once the grip comes off.
cells.sheetLine: Care has turned into holding on, and it's exhausting you both.

cells.tense: The door was left open a long time ago, and you're still standing at it.
cells.act: move toward the thing you actually want
cells.ask: Go a small step toward what draws you — no plan, no announcing, nobody told. The step is everything here.
cells.core:
You keep things going. You handle it, you don't need help, and the ones close to you have learned that. Meanwhile something has gone quiet in you — a thing you used to grow, that hasn't moved in a while. You've said it was fine. Anyone near would be startled to hear that said plainly.

Begin with something you want. Go a small step toward it this week, and nothing beyond that — no plan to justify it, nobody informed. Not what duty points at; what pulls, even a little. Letting go here isn't a large push, it's turning your face from a door you already walked through. Do that much and watch what it does to the room you've kept shut.

cells.tense: You're holding this up, and you'd tell it as simply being good at it.
cells.act: stop holding what no longer serves
cells.ask: Set down a burden that isn't yours — a worry, a keeping-going, an arrangement — and don't say a word that you did.
cells.core:
People come to you. Some of what you carry was chosen once, and a lot arrived because you kept agreeing, and because of that you're tired in a way you don't bring up. Yours is the caring hand. Asked about it, you'd say you're good at it, or needed, or that things would fall apart without you.

Set down, for a week, a single weight that was never really yours. Don't announce it, don't explain it, don't fill the place where it sat. That week is the experiment. You'll learn what happens to it and to you — and what doesn't happen — which is knowledge you can't reach with both arms full.
cells.sheetLine: Anyone leans on you, and you've named it as being capable.
